column1: # Direct AST record construction in test sources — a ratchet, not a register.
# Each row is a file's remaining budget of `new <AstRecord>(…)` calls. The published
# builders (AstBuilders/Expr/ScriptBuilders) are how a test should build a node; these
# are what predates them. AstConstructionRatchetTest holds every file to its row:
#   * a file with no row must have NO direct construction — this is what stops new ones;
#   * a file with a row must not exceed it — this is what stops the old ones spreading;
#   * a file BELOW its row fails, asking for the row to be tightened — which is what
#     makes "migrate what you touch" a thing the build records rather than a thing
#     people remember. A budget that only ever ratchets down cannot drift back up.
# So: migrate the file you are already editing, then lower or delete its row in the
# same commit. Deleting the last row is the end of the migration.
# The deliberate effort to spend these budgets down — what is mechanical, where it
# stops, and in what order — is defined in issue #780. Nothing obliges anyone to
# start it: the ratchet already guarantees the number cannot grow.
# Some rows will never reach zero, and that is correct: a test whose subject IS the
# record — its canonical constructor, its validation, its location component — has to
# call the constructor. The builders default SourceLocation to UNKNOWN and none takes
# one, so a test asserting on positions cannot use them either.
# The exemption attaches to the RECORD, not to the file, and six files are where the
# migration has deliberately stopped short. In each, the named record's own constructor
# is what is being asserted on — its guards, its accessors, its defensive copying — so
# a factory in front of it would test the factory:
#   AstNodeUnaryTest          LimitNode          (its asc/desc fixtures are migrated)
#   AstNodeRelationTest       the relation and join nodes
#   AstValidationTest         every constructor it guards
#   AstPredicateOperandTest   ElementOfPredicate, SortSpecification
#   SessionizeNodeTest        SessionizeNode
#   TreeNodeTest              TreeNode           (its asc/desc fixtures are migrated)
#   ClosureNodeTest, ClusterNodeTest, PathNodeTest, CoverNodeTest, FixpointNodeTest,
#     TraceNodeTest, WhyNodeTest, WindowNodeTest, OuterUnionNodeTest,
#     EmptyRelationNodeTest, TruthRelationNodeTest, ConditionalJoinNodeTest — each its
#     own node
#   ProduceBoundTest          ProduceBound
#   RelationFunctionCallTest  RelationFunctionCall
#   AggregateFunctionTest     AggregateFunction
#   LangAstSourceTest         InlineTableBody
#   LangAstScriptTest         ImportStatement, DefStatement
#   LangAstValidationTest     DefRelationStatement, JsonFileSourceConfig, RelateStatement
# Three more stay for reasons of their own:
#   AstLocations (testFixtures) rebuilds every record with a stripped location — it is
#     constructor code by construction, and no factory takes a location.
#   ScriptCorpus / ScriptCorpusTest / ScriptCorpusRoundTripTest hold one instance of each
#     statement kind. Built through the factories, the corpus would assert the factories.
#   TypeTest builds StructType.Field, which lives in relix-symbol — below the builders in
#     the module graph, so no factory can reach it.
#   FunctionCatalogContractTest builds `new FunctionCall(name, args)` from two variables.
#     `func` is varargs, and a List that arrives as a variable cannot be spliced into one.
# With those recorded, every remaining row is one of the above. The rules that got here
# are in tools/ast-builders/literal_rewrite.py; `--rule all` re-runs them, and a row that
# drops is a row the tool will tighten for you.
# A SortSpecification inside a TreeNode test is fixture data and was migrated; the
# TreeNode around it was not. `literal_rewrite.py --except <Kind>` is how that line is
# drawn on a re-run.
